correctness.rationale: Independently project the central section onto the yz-square. For sorted a≥b≥c, a>c, the same-sign quadrants each lose a corner triangle of area (b+c)^2/[2(a+b)(a+c)], and the opposite-sign quadrants each lose (b−c)^2/[2(a+b)(a−c)]. For the former quadrants the cut-line intercepts on the sides of the square both obey |by+cz|≤a; for the latter quadrants this slab bound is automatic and the inequality from the other sign of by+cz is redundant. Multiplying the remaining area by ||u||/a yields the stated formula, including ties short of the body diagonal. The derivative numerator N(s,r) strictly decreases in r<s² for s>0 and has nonnegative endpoint 6s(1−s)^2; the diagonal-envelope log derivative is positive for s>0. The lower-envelope squared difference is s³[4(1−s²)+s+s³], strictly positive for 0<s≤1. At a=b=c the central section is a regular hexagon, and the path c=b attains the whole interval between the two extrema. Evenness and Brunn concavity reduce the affine maximum to the central one and force a body-diagonal normal at equality. Independently, at 0≤h≤2 the diagonal section is the slice of [h/2−1,1]^3 at sum h: singleton negative-sum inequalities give the lower bounds and pair inequalities follow from x_i≤1. After translation the cube has side m=2−h/2 and the sum is s=m+1. The simplex-area inclusion-exclusion gives √3(s²−3)/2, the stated profile; it decreases strictly, has a triangular facet at h=2 and no section beyond. This proves the full affine equality assertion and handles the degenerate cases.
residual_risks: The finite replay is corroboration; the continuum conclusions rely on the geometry, derivative signs and Brunn concavity. No area profile for nonmaximizing affine directions is claimed.

value.rationale: A natural sharp slicing problem for a standard solid. The exact directional law is useful beyond a single benchmark: it identifies a strict balancing mechanism, classifies both central extrema, and resolves possible noncentral equality with a full profile in the maximizing orientation. The maximizing direction differs from the ordinary cube benchmark. None of the area or equality information follows just from the existing side counts.
residual_risks: No transfer to arbitrary truncation depths, other dimensions, or nonmaximizing-direction offset profiles is asserted.
